card.name: Turning-point words in narrative asides
card.fires_on: Words in short pivot phrases in news or opinion prose that introduce a catch, an ironic aside, or a turn in the story. Examples are "just one problem", "Never mind that", "except for the", "That's when" and "never mention".

modes.label: Catch or problem
modes.description: The word right after a setup that introduces a catch or complication.
modes.example: There’s just one<< problem>>: the DNA tests and related treatments have

modes.label: Dismissive or ironic aside
modes.description: Words after "Never mind", "No matter" or "never" that brush aside a fact.
modes.example: Never mind<< that>> the temporary inconvenience of a largely harmless infection

modes.label: Casual quoted remark
modes.description: Words in a spoken understatement beginning "That part wasn't so much fun".
modes.example: ("That part wasn<<'t>> so much fun," says Dr. Ber
